ai.description: *Mysticellus franki* is a small, stout frog reaching 30 mm. It is brown with a dark, X-shaped dorsal mark and a distinct, pale-edged black spot on each flank. It lacks visible tympana.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Mysticellus franki* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, dark, butterfly-shaped marking on the dorsum, which is absent in other similar Indian narrow-mouthed frogs.
ai.habitat: *Mysticellus franki* inhabits the leaf litter of moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Mysticellus franki* is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by inflating its body and emitting a loud, high-pitched distress call when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Mysticellus franki* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in temporary pools. They exhibit explosive breeding behavior typical of narrow-mouthed frogs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Mysticellus franki* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits mid-elevation forests between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Mysticellus franki* is a high-pitched, rapid series of metallic chirps heard primarily during the monsoon season in leaf litter near temporary forest pools.
